newsitem.title: USA: Star witness takes stand in Oklahoma bomb trial.
newsitem.headline: Star witness takes stand in Oklahoma bomb trial.

text.p: The star prosecution witness in the Oklahoma City bombing trial testified Monday that he and accused bomber Timothy McVeigh thought "somebody should be held accountable" for the deaths of 80 cult members at Waco, Texas.

McVeigh's former Army buddy Michael Fortier, 28, told a hushed Denver courtroom how McVeigh grew increasingly angry over the April 19, 1993, confrontation between federal agents and Branch Davidian cult members at Waco which ended in the cultists' deaths.
Fortier, a friend of McVeigh who lived in Kingman, Arizona, has pleaded guilty to four felony counts in return to testifying that he knew about plans for the bombing but did nothing to stop it.
He is expected to be the government's key witness in its case against McVeigh, who is accused of bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City, killing 168 people.

Fortier testified that he and McVeigh had many discussions about the Waco confrontation in 1993. "We both concluded the federal government had intentionally attacked those people...potentially they murdered those people in Waco," he said.
In later discussions about Waco, the two men expressed their belief that the Branch Davidians were murdered "and that there was a coverup, that somebody should be held accountable."
